AP labeled five promises “Kept,” nine “In progress” and 11 “It’s complicated.” The categories cover issues including immigration, education, energy, foreign policy, government, health care, taxes and tariffs. proposed_title: AP’s Tracker Categorized 25 Selected Trump Campaign Promises by Status
description_medium: AP’s tracker data last modified Dec. 3, 2025, covered 25 selected campaign promises. It labeled five “Kept,” nine “In progress” and 11 “It’s complicated.” The file supports a dated count of AP’s categories, but not a separate measure of campaign certainty versus governing throughput. The snapshot covers only the promises AP selected for tracking.
description_long: The Associated Press tracker data retrieved for this review contains 25 selected promises from Donald Trump’s 2024 campaign. The dataset’s last-modified field is Dec. 3, 2025. AP assigned five entries the label “Kept,” nine “In progress” and 11 “It’s complicated.” Individual rows identify the promise, its policy category and a status; many include links to related AP reporting, and some link to executive actions or other government materials. The dataset therefore provides a dated accounting of how AP categorized those particular promises at that time. It does not supply a single quantitative measure called governing throughput, explain a broad method for comparing campaign certainty with implementation pace, or establish a current status after December 2025. Nor does a count of tracker labels show that Trump’s public delivery narrative depended on selected wins. A defensible description can report the tracker’s scope, timestamp and category totals, while treating the labels as AP’s status ratings rather than a comprehensive score of presidential performance.
